note: Balanced curated accounts; leans describe the account, not each post. Midterms 2026 post-election window.

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
Last night was the largest blue wave in a generation.

Democrats have been projected as winner in 54 Senate seats, flipping seven states and with a lead in two others (Alaska and Mississippi).

In the House, Democrats have been projected in 249 seats - a net gain of 38 so far.

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
Decision Desk HQ projects Jon Ossoff wins the GA US Senate General Election

#DecisionMade: 7:18 PM EST

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
DDHQ FORECAST UPDATE (11/3): FINAL UPDATE

Our final forecast gives Democrats an 84% probability of winning the House, with a seat total of 241.

In the Senate, Democrats have a 64% probability of winning a majority of seats, with a projected total of 52 seats.

posts.name: G Elliott Morris
posts.text: FINAL forecast: Will it be a blue wave, or a blue tsunami? Democrats favored to win 240 House and 52-53 Senate seats on average. Polling error could be enough for Rs to hold the Senate, but House would need biggest miss in 25 years

posts.name: G Elliott Morris
posts.text: Black voter turnout held at ~96% of 2024, the highest rate for any midterm in at least a decade, in the Deep South on Tues. If Scott Colom manages to win Mississippi's Senate seat, it wouldn't have been possible without sky-high engagement of Black voters

posts.name: Cook Political Report
posts.text:
Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats, including five that voted for Trump by double digits. In the House, Democrats are en route to their largest majority of the century.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: Fully newsletter is here. I also get into the Q of *when* the results might be known. Typically, we'd expect 1-2 Senate races and 10-15 House races to be *uncalled* as of early Wednesday morning. Alaska and Maine are slow to count their votes.

posts.name: Aaron Rupar
posts.text: Jake Tapper laughs as Kaitlan Collins reads the White House statement absurdly absolving Trump of blame for tonight's blue wave

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: Even a very Republican-skewing judicial branch has been a meaningful check on Trump and flipping the senate — and only flipping the senate — stops Trump from stacking the judiciary with cultists who'll remove that check.

posts.name: CNN Politics
posts.text: Democratic state Rep. James Talarico will win the Senate race in Texas, CNN projects, delivering a stunning defeat to Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton. Talarico is the first Democrat elected to represent Texas in the US Senate in 38 years.

posts.name: CNN Politics
posts.text: Democrats are projected to oust at least 30 Republican incumbents in this year's midterms, surpassing 250 House seats on the party's way to its largest majority since the 2008 election.

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: For the last two years, the Trump Administration has been governed by a simple mantra: “We can just do things.” On Tuesday, voters replied, “So can we,” and wiped out the GOP. This was not a blue wave. This was not a blue tsunami. This was the breakup of a winning coalition.

posts.name: Byron York

posts.text: Were I a ranking Republican in the House or Senate, I’d start taking the Trump family corruption seriously and cooperate in grown up investigations.  90% of voters said corruption was a determining factor in their vote and over 60% pointed not to Somali fraud or highspeed rail,

posts.name: POLITICO
posts.text:
Every part of the country is shifting toward Dems — a sign of the "blue wave" Republicans had long feared.

Democratic candidates’ gains in House and Senate races cut across both blue and red territory, along with traditional purple battlegrounds.

posts.name: POLITICO
posts.text: 🚨Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper beat Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina’s Senate race, becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate election in the state in nearly two decades.
